bullets.short: Serving as a lead on the ground-up build-out of Rho's San Francisco headquarters — driving construction sequencing, space layout design, and amenity program across 3 floors with no general contractor, coordinating 15+ vendors and contractors simultaneously
bullets.detail: Rho's SF headquarters required a complete ground-up build-out across three floors with no general contractor overseeing the work, so vendor sequencing and dependency management were owned internally. I help lead construction sequencing, space layout, and the amenity program while coordinating 15+ vendors and contractors at once. When a structural blocker on Floor 3 made the planned electrical approach infeasible, I researched and proposed a surface-mounted alternative that preserved the timeline. The project is on track for substantial completion with concurrent workstreams progressing without coordination-driven delays.

bullets.short: Designing and executing the full SF workplace experience — space planning, kitchen and amenity installation, AV infrastructure, signage, and furniture coordination — taking the office from shell to fully operational
bullets.detail: Beyond construction, I own the experiential layer of the office: how the space looks, feels, and functions on day one. That spans space planning, kitchen and amenity installation, AV infrastructure, signage, and furniture coordination — translating design intent into installed reality. I make on-the-ground material and placement decisions in real time when the design firm isn't present, keeping the build moving. The result is an office built from empty shell to fully operational without a dedicated project-management firm.

bullets.short: Driving cost optimization through contractor negotiations and creative problem-solving on build issues, consistently bringing proposals in under initial estimates and eliminating unnecessary change orders
bullets.detail: With 15+ vendors and no dedicated finance oversight, controlling spend was a core part of the role rather than an afterthought. I disputed a ~$9K electrical overquote by pushing for pricing transparency and identified ~$5K in savings by relocating electrical work on Floor 3. I also resolved a 44-fixture lighting delivery error with the vendor and electrician at no incremental cost while preserving UL certification. Across the project I consistently brought proposals in under initial estimates and eliminated unnecessary change orders.

bullets.short: Led end-to-end remodel of a modular event space — managed AV installation, secured electrical permits through the City of San Francisco, sourced and procured furniture via cross-country travel, and delivered the project $30K under budget; the space supports All-Hands, off-sites, and client events for 200+ employees
bullets.detail: Klaviyo's SF hub event space needed to flex between All-Hands, off-sites, and client-facing events for 200+ employees, which meant rethinking AV, layout, and furniture together. I led the remodel end-to-end — managing AV installation, securing electrical permits through the City of San Francisco, and traveling cross-country to source and procure the right furniture. By sourcing strategically and managing the vendor relationships directly, I delivered the full project $30K under budget. The finished space materially expanded how the office could be used without a larger build-out.

bullets.short: Designed the SF office environment including art curation and a full plant program, creating a biophilic, brand-aligned workplace that elevated the daily employee experience
bullets.detail: Beyond the event space, I shaped the broader feel of the SF office through art curation and a full plant program. The goal was a biophilic, brand-aligned environment that made the office somewhere people actively wanted to be, not just a place to work. These are the details that shape day-to-day employee experience even when they're not consciously noticed.

bullets.detail: Operating inside an enterprise real-estate footprint meant managing relationships with major landlords and operators — CBRE, Knotel, and WeWork — alongside Klaviyo's own contractors. I oversaw outside contractors and partnered with building security and safety teams on access control, inspections, and emergency response protocols. This is the less visible side of workplace operations: keeping the building's systems and the company's needs aligned.

That meant balancing high-touch concierge support for the CFO, HR, and Marketing leads with the steady operational needs of the broader team. The role demanded constant prioritization and independent judgment — knowing what to handle immediately, what to schedule, and what to escalate.

bullets.detail: In-office attendance was lagging, so I treated it as an experience problem rather than a mandate problem. I launched a break-room concessions program and a set of in-office engagement initiatives designed around what actually brought people in. The combination increased on-site attendance by 35% and noticeably strengthened day-to-day culture.

The switch reduced annual spend by $15K and worked well enough that the company adopted it across all locations.

bullets.detail: Across two sites in SF and San Mateo, I owned the AV and IT infrastructure that meeting spaces depend on — conference room AV, Zoom-enabled rooms, network, print, and digital signage. The priority was reliability: making sure the technology never became the reason a meeting didn't start on time. I'm not a dedicated IT specialist, but I'm comfortable owning these systems operationally and partnering with IT on deeper technical work.
